specification.problem: Decompose a general bipartite unitary on C^{d_A} ⊗ C^{d_B} into a product of controlled unitaries (controlled from A, targeting B), with the gate-count bounds stated in the abstract. Only the counting bounds are explicit; the construction itself is not in the abstract.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scope: the bipartite controlled-unitary decomposition form and its stated gate-count bounds, plus the tiny instance d_A=2, d_B=2. Outside scope: the explicit decomposition construction, the complex permutation result with three controlled unitaries, the n-partite bound proof, the local-unitary plus simple-gate decomposition, the CNOT/entanglement cost bounds via Schmidt rank, and the log-rank / nonnegative rank connection.

symbols.meaning: dimension of the control system A
dimension of the target system B
k-th controlled unitary, block diagonal in a fixed A basis
unitary on B applied when A is in basis state i in the k-th gate
number of controlled unitaries in the decomposition

equations.label: Controlled unitary form
equations.description: General form of a controlled unitary with control A and target B, in a fixed computational basis of A.
equations.justification: Standard definition of a controlled unitary; the abstract does not give its explicit form.
assumptions: The control basis is the computational basis of A.
Controlled unitaries are controlled from A onto B.

equations.label: Decomposition form
equations.description: Any bipartite unitary is a product of N controlled unitaries.
equations.abstract_quote: any unitary operator on the $d_{A}\times d_{B}$ system ($d_{A}\geq 2$) can be decomposed into the product of at most $4d_{A}-5$ controlled unitary operators
equations.justification: Inferred from the claim of a product of controlled unitaries. The control direction may alternate between A and B in the actual method; this is not stated.
assumptions: Which system controls each factor is not specified in the abstract.

equations.label: General bound
equations.description: Upper bound on the number of controlled unitaries for general d_A.

equations.label: Power-of-two bound
equations.description: Reduced bound when d_A is a power of two.
equations.abstract_quote: The number can be reduced to $2d_{A}-1$ when $d_{A}$ is a power of two
assumptions: The bound is read as an upper bound, consistent with the preceding 'at most'.

equations.label: n-partite bound
equations.description: Bound for n-partite unitaries, each gate controlled from n-1 systems.
equations.justification: Stated in the abstract; listed for context only and outside the construction scope.

steps.description: Fix the computational bases of A and B and the target unitary U on C^{d_A} ⊗ C^{d_B}.
Write the decomposition as a product of N controlled unitaries of the form in eq_1, with N within the bounds of eq_3 or eq_4. For d_A=2 the bound is N<=3 (=2d_A-1).
The explicit choice of the V_{k,i} and the control direction of each factor is not derivable from the abstract and must come from the paper.

assumptions: Tiny instance d_A=d_B=2 chosen by me as the smallest useful case.
Controlled unitaries are taken to be block diagonal in a computational basis of the control system.
The decomposition is treated as an exact operator identity.
